section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "Tzion will be redeemed through justice and her captives through charity," and the Rebbe Rashab's question about the meaning of "Tzion" and "her captives."
section.t: "Tzion will be redeemed through justice, and her captives through charity."
And the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" of the year 5666,
notes that the intention of "Tzion" here is not the city of Tzion
[specifically]
but rather
[the collective]
of Israel,
and [asks] why does it say "Tzion."
And he also notes what is written "and her captives," etc.,
who are the captives.
[And it can be said,
that this note as well
(who are the captives)
is based on what was said before, that the intention of "Tzion" here is the collective of Israel.
For there are commentators
that "Tzion" refers to the city of Tzion and "her captives" refers to Israel.
But according to the interpretation
(in the maamar)
that "Tzion" refers to Israel,
what are the two categories of "Tzion" and "her captives"?]
And also, what is the concept that the redemption of Tzion will be through justice and the redemption of the captives through charity.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Tzion" refers to those involved in Torah and mitzvos, while "her captives" are those not involved in Torah, and their respective redemptions are through justice and charity.
section.t: And the point of the explanation
(according to what is explained in the Reshimos of the Tzemach Tzedek on the verse
and in the aforementioned maamar),
is that "Tzion" refers to Israel who engage in Torah and mitzvos,
and they are called by the name "Tzion" because they are distinguished in Torah and mitzvos.
[And as it is brought in the Yerushalmi
on the verse
"And I have placed My words in your mouth and with the shadow of My hand I have covered you, to plant the heavens and to lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Tzion, 'You are My people,'"
we searched through all of Scripture and did not find that Israel is called "Tzion" except this
(that it is said)
"and to say to Tzion, 'You are My people.'"
And the explanation of this is known,
that this verse speaks of the three things upon which the world stands,
Torah, service, and acts of kindness.
"And I have placed My words in your mouth" — this is Torah,
"and with the shadow of My hand I have covered you" — this is acts of kindness,
"to plant the heavens and to lay the foundations of the earth" — these are the offerings
(as it is brought in the Yerushalmi there).
And this is [the meaning of] "we did not find that Israel is called Tzion except this,"
because this [name] that Israel is called by the name "Tzion" is through their engagement in Torah, service, and acts of kindness,
which are the entirety of all Torah and mitzvos.]
And "her captives" are those who do not engage in Torah,
who are literally in captivity
[and "captives" (shiveha) is from the term captivity (shivyah)]
in body and the animal soul.
And this is [the meaning of] "Tzion will be redeemed through justice and her captives through charity,"
that the redemption of those who engage in Torah is through justice,
according to the line of law,
in contrast, the redemption of the captives is in the manner of charity.
And although even the redemption of those who are in captivity in body and animal soul will be through repentance,
for Israel are not redeemed except through repentance
and the Torah promised that ultimately Israel will repent at the end of their exile and
(through this)
they are immediately redeemed
[And it can be said,
that this is the connection of the interpretation of "her captives" from the term captivity with the interpretation that "her captives" (shoveha) are those who repent
(and "her captives" is from the term repentance (teshuvah)),
because the redemption of the captives, from the term captivity, is through their doing repentance],
nevertheless, that repentance atones is not according to justice,
but rather it is the kindness and charity of the Holy One, blessed be He.
However, even so,
the redemption of the captives is higher than the redemption of Tzion,
because the concept of justice is measure and limitation,
in contrast, charity is beyond limitation.
And as is explained in the maamar,
that justice is the light that is within the category of vessels,
and charity is the light that is in the differentiation that comes only in a manner of charity.
Therefore,
the light that is drawn to the righteous, whose redemption is through justice,
is the light that is within the category of vessels.
[And this is that what [it means that] their redemption is through justice,
there are two aspects to this.
One,
that they do not need charity,
because it is coming to them according to law.
Two,
that the concept of justice precludes charity,
as it is written
"You shall not show favor in judgment,"
and Rashi explains
that you should not say this one is poor, etc., and it is a mitzvah to support him].
And the light that is drawn to the penitents, whose redemption is through charity,
is the light that is in the differentiation.
